## Intent
Hypothesis: compiler auto-vectorization over per-particle components can approach the streaming ceiling on death-free workloads.

## Layout & approach
The 68 B/particle AoS layout gives sequential access but only 47% hot bytes in loop 1 (32 of 68: age+pos+seed+vel) and 41% in loop 2 (28 of 68: color+pos) — the rest is dead cacheline weight. No intermediate storage keeps the death verdict in registers but leaves a branchy per-particle loop the compiler cannot flatten. All measured N (10K–10M) are L3-resident or DRAM.

## Cache saturation
At q=0.01, cost is flat at 7.7 ns/p in L3 (N=10K–100K), then rises ~43% to 10.6–11.0 ns/p in DRAM (N≥1M) — the knee matches the L3 spill at N≈246K. At q=0.5 the same two-regime shape holds but the DRAM rise shrinks to ~9% (17.4→18.9 ns/p): branchy-respawn compute dominates memory latency, masking the spill.

## Bandwidth
The floor is 5.359 ns/p. At q=0.01 in L3: 7.7 ns/p (1.44× floor), 8.82 GB/s = 69.5% of the 12.69 ceiling. In DRAM: 6.2–6.4 GB/s (49–51%). At q=0.5: 3.6–3.9 GB/s (28–31%). The algo is frontend-bound: frontend stalls 59–75%, backend ≤0.1%, branch_flush 0.0% — the 304-instruction footprint starves the decoder, not the memory bus. vs baseline: 0.30× at q=0.01 (3.3× faster than naive), 0.50–0.55× at q=0.5 (1.8–2.0× faster) — branchy respawn is the equalizer. vs winner: 1.0× everywhere — this IS the winner.

## Assembly
No cross-particle vectorization: the loop advances r14 by 0x44 per iteration (one particle), vector-suffixed instructions = 0. Packed ops (vmulps, vaddps, vpaddusb) handle 3-component vectors within one particle. Integration uses vmovups, vmovsd, then vmulss/vshufps/vinsertps/vmulps/vaddps. Death check is branchy (vucomiss+jae+jne+jnp, call to spawn). Render does byte-granular scatter: movzx+add+cmovb+mov BYTE PTR per channel, vpaddusb on the fast path. No gather; sequential AoS is prefetch-friendly but the 304-instruction mix is too heavy to stream.

## Verdict
Partially holds — winner at every point (1.0×) and 3.3× faster than naive at q=0.01 (0.30× baseline), 1.8–2.0× at q=0.5 (0.50–0.55× baseline). But it never approaches the ceiling: 69.5% at best (q=0.01, L3), 28–31% at q=0.5. The compiler emitted no cross-particle vectorization (vector-suffixed=0, one particle per iteration); the win comes from scalar-SSE efficiency and register-resident verdicts. Frontend stalls (59–75%) from the 304-instruction branchy footprint cap bandwidth below the ceiling at all death rates.
